replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a quadratic equation ax²+bx+c=0: 1) Identify coefficients a,b,c. 2) Calculate discriminant Δ=b²-4ac. 3) Apply quadratic formula x=(-b±√Δ)/(2a). 4) If Δ>0, two real roots exist; if Δ=0, one repeated root; if Δ<0, complex conjugate roots emerge.

To locate stationary points: 1) Compute derivative dy/dx. 2) Set derivative equal to zero and solve for x values. 3) Substitute each x back into original function to find corresponding y coordinates. 4) Use second derivative test: if d²y/dx²>0 it's a minimum, <0 maximum, or zero indicates potential inflection point.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces dimensions by finding orthogonal axes maximizing variance. Steps: 1) Standardize data to have zero mean and unit variance. 2) Compute covariance matrix. 3) Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors. 4) Sort eigenvectors by eigenvalues descending. 5) Project original data onto top k eigenvectors. Don't worry; the math builds on linear algebra fundamentals you already know.
